proof_summary: For even inputs, a positive representation directly gives the Goldbach decomposition \(n=(n-q)+q\), while for odd inputs it gives the Lemoine decomposition \(n=(n-2q)+2q\); direct finite searches establish all cases below the respective thresholds. For any bound \(N\), applying the hypothesis to \(n=2N+8014\) produces a witness with \(2q<n\), so \(p=n-q\) has \(p-6>N\), and the primality of \(p-6\) and \(p\) gives arbitrarily large cousin-prime pairs.
